Alien: Isolation is a game that punishes you for thinking you’re in control. The difficulty is relentless, and that’s what makes it so brilliant. The xenomorph isn’t a scripted enemy — it’s a predator that learns from your mistakes, adapts, and ruthlessly punishes any hint of confidence. You think you’re safe? Wrong. You think you’ve saved? Don’t get too comfortable.

Stealth isn’t a choice — it’s everything. The slightest sound could mean your death, so you’ll spend more time crouching in the dark, holding your breath, than doing anything remotely heroic. Running? Forget it. You’re not fast enough, and the alien’s got your number. Even the crafting system — a rare moment of control — is fraught with tension as you scramble for resources while wondering which vent will be your grave.

I've played on difficulty and it's punishing, but it’s fair. Every mistake feels like it could be your last, and you’ll absolutely scream in panic more times than you can count.

9/10 – The hardest, most terrifying game of cat-and-mouse you’ll ever play.

This game follows a sine curve of fun.

The first hour and a half of gameplay is incredibly slow and boring.

Then when you meet the alien the game becomes extremely tense and fun and terror-inspiring.

Then when you meet the cyborgs the game becomes boring and predictable again.

Then the game's closing acts pick up the pace once again and give a very satisfying conclusion.

Overall, I definitely recommend it. I can't think of another game that's able to create such an amazing degree of suspense and pure animal horror like this game. The atmosphere and storytelling are excellent as well.

Finally, a game that does the Alien universe justice. I just finished my first play through on Hard and it was a thrill ride through and through. Above all, the art work and atmosphere was *incredible*. If I could shake the hands of the developers, I would. They mastered the look, feel, and sound of the original movie.
I recommend it to anyone looking for a tense, atmospheric horror game, especially if they're an Alien fan.
A welcome addition to the Alien universe.

Good game with a tense atmosphere, but I wouldn't call it scary (at least it wasn't for me). Also be aware that this is by no means an action game. Also, because of the nature of the game, you will have to crawl (at a snail's pace) your way back to places you have done before, because you got killed by the alien while you were reading something on one of the many computers, for example. It can become aggravating because, even though there is a fair amount of save points, going places generally involves nothing but crawling which is, again, very slow.

However it's worth playing if you enjoy stealth games or the Alien franchise. If you can get the GOTY edition for under 15$ it's quite a bargain, too.

I should probably mention that I played on the hardest setting, so some of the things I mentionned might not be an issue for everyone.

The only 2 issues I have with the game are that it's a bit too long, and it becomes significantly less scary after you acquire the flamethrower. Not a perfect game but I still liked it despite my criticisms. 8/10 for me.

Stealing an idea I saw done here to help me get through my huge backlog of games on Steam. It is what I like to call my "1 Hour Playtime Reviews Because My Steam Library Has Gotten Stupid Big and I Don't Want to Regret How I Spend My Money Challenge."

Alien Isolation is that time when I realize another downside to the 1 hour part of this whole ordeal. Unlike an earlier game on the list: About Love, Hate and the Other Ones, an hour was not enough time. I wanted to keep playing really bad.

The game is tense from the moment it starts and the lack of real direction and this feeling of great danger around every corner makes exploring and pressing on a constantly frightful endeavor. It introduces characters and the story so far has been your typical Alien fare done well.

Exploring the environments feels like you're walking around the set and even though I didn't get far enough to run into the Xenomorph itself, what I have seen already is building a good sense of tension and danger. Just like any good horror game, every damn save point is a gasp of relief, and yeah, maybe I saved it twice everytime out of some weird sense of security.

Excellent atmosphere and tension building. Alien has a pretty cool universe, and this game does such a good job of making you feel as afraid as Ripley is in that universe. It's just so faithful to the films and the established world. Truly impressive work. My only real complaint is that, while playing on Normal difficulty, I wasn't always sure what the advantages of some items were when compared to others. I didn't use the grenade item once because I never really made it my mission to outright assault anything, and if I wanted to attract attention I would just use a noisemaker or even a smoke bomb. Again, there probably aren't as many options in higher difficulties, but I don't think that's much of an excuse.

When it comes to survival horror, Alien Isolation hits so many checkboxes. It immerses you in a world that feels authentic to the original Alien movie, which also means being hunted by the horrible Xenomorph. No place feels safe and every area in the game keeps you on edge. I do not particularly enjoy horror games, but Alien Isolation keeps me coming back to cautiously traverse the tight corridors of the Sevastapol with a gleeful fear.

This is one of the best horror/suspense games ever made. It captures the atmosphere of the Alien world perfectly. As an Alien fan, I regard this story as "part 3" in the Alien saga, after Alien and Aliens (all other movies being forgettable, at best).

The acting, storyline, graphics and sound are all top-notch and it is hard to find any fault at all in the entire game. If I HAD to be picky, I would say the only thing that stood out as a slightly weaker element was the movement of the Alien itself. It’s just a subtle thing, but I think its movement could have been slightly more in keeping with the first two movies.

Overall though, if you want an Alien experience on your PC, this is it!

But is the game scary? Well, if you're not familiar with the series AT ALL it very well might be but I think most people know about the series, everyone has seen the Xenomorph, incredibly iconic design but not scary at this point, it may be a bit startling in the beggining as you're learning how the AI works, the first proper encounter with it in that medical area is pretty good and has some tension but dies off pretty quick.

If you can get it for like 10 bucks or less I'd say it's worth it just for the first third of the game but not full price in my opinion.

I don't like horror movies; nor I have any kind of preference toward horror games. I'm a gentle heart person, easily scared by... well, almost everything.

But this game... O boy! It's a full, complete, total masochistic experience where you know that you have to be scared at least a couple of times to really enjoy it. And the good thing is that you haven't to do anything special, apart from actually sit down in front of your bare metal. Even if your poor Amanda remains completely still without explore the ship, IT will finds her.

No, not the killer clown. The Xeno. That's worse.

And the Xeno will adapt itself in a scientific (statistical) manner. You have to vary your strategies or the Xeno will always catch you. Be unpredictable!

Now, keep calm & git this game -> better on sales, because it's a 2014 title.

I'm a huge fan of the Alien movie, and I have to say I might like this even more than the movie. It has a gripping and terrifying story, with what's in my opinion excellently executed gameplay. It has genuinely frightening environments even in areas without any bodies or enemies, and my favorite thing about the environment is that they kept the design language exactly the same as the Alien movie. The technology in Alien is such an interesting mix of old and new, and I think they nailed it in the game between the sound effects, the hardware design, and the software design. Also, Being that there's really not any large open environments, that gives the game a huge performance benefit (my overclocked GTX 860m can run it on ultra with hardly ever dropping below 60fps at 1080p). If you're a fan of the original Alien movie, I'd definitely pick up this game.

This is a hide and seek game, that masterfully captures the idea of the first Alien movie. If you like the Xenomorph, or like stealth games, I certainly reccomend this game.

Be mindful, however:
- This is not an FPS. You will spend most of your time hiding.
- If you don't understand how the alien searches, you will get killed A LOT.
- You will spend a lot of time against other enemies as well.
- The DLCs: Crew expendable & Last survivor are REALLY short. they are, however, really fun for fans since they let you play the Alien Movie Story (Ellen Ripley & crew)

First person game in which fear is part of the whole game. You will have to hide and go through dark rooms and hallways of space ships and space stations, where an aggressive alien will hunt you, using the air conditioning ducts ... You will also have to fight with very violent androids and humans, who will be an obstacle to complete each of the missions

Pros:
-One of the best horror games I have played.
-The graphics are really good.
-The atmosphere is scary and creepy.
-It is SO well done on how the tech and whatnot are LIKE in the movies!
-Scary Alien and Androids.
-Really great sound/music design.
-Makes you super paranoid and it is done perfectly!

Cons:
-Some parts of the missions feel like they lasted too long. Killing the mood.
-Few bugs here and there. The main one I encountered was visual clitches where some object started to make the screen black or something in that direction. Only encountered it a couple times.
-The alien following you EVERYWHERE gets annoying!
-Parts here and there have to be done is a certain way and if you don't realize it, you are going to die quite a bit.

It is a horror games that those that love horror games should at least give a try. Some parts get annoying and you might die a lot but overall a great experience.

Okay, so I'm not that far into the story yet... The reason why?
Actually it's a good thing (depending on how you look at it)...
I can't progress through (*SPOILERS ALERT*) the medbay to get a keycard, not because there's a glitch or anything but simply because this freakin' game scares the crap out of me. Xenomorphs aren't the friendliest of creatures even when armed with a pulse rifle and whatnot but when all you have is some simple revolver and a maintenance jack... you are absolutely powerless against it and the fear is real. So to put it simply, I cannot progress because I crap my pants everytime.

To be honest, this game truly deserves the awards it has won. I'm not saying this because I am a huge fan of the franchise but heck, the atmosphere this game builds, the fear factor, the way it controls, the way the Alien moves, everything about it, is excellent. And to top it off, it looks god damn beautiful! The lighting, the textures, the sounds, it's all god damn gorgeous.

Would I recommend this game? Hell yes, 10/10.
Will you crap your pants? Most definitely!

This game is dark and should be played in dark room. If you dare to try it :)
